rationale: The earlier fix filtered the edit view by permissions, but it assumed the global permission policy was always bound to the active document model. When WAGTAILDOCS_DOCUMENT_MODEL is swapped at runtime, the global policy can still point at the default model, so its permission-filtered queryset didn’t contain custom documents, causing 404s. The queryset logic now reuses the base queryset, rebuilds a compatible permission policy when needed, and intersects it with the permitted IDs, ensuring both permission filtering and compatibility with custom document models.
patch:
diff --git a/wagtail/documents/views/documents.py b/wagtail/documents/views/documents.py
index fe948f6907..6dee40f98d 100644
--- a/wagtail/documents/views/documents.py
+++ b/wagtail/documents/views/documents.py
@@ -218,11 +218,29 @@ class EditView(generic.EditView):
 return get_document_model()
 
 def get_queryset(self):
+ queryset = super().get_queryset()
 if not self.permission_policy or not self.permission_required:
- return super().get_queryset()
- return self.permission_policy.instances_user_has_permission_for(
+ return queryset
+
+ policy = self.permission_policy
+ if policy.model is not self.model:
+ init_kwargs = {}
+ if hasattr(policy, "_auth_model_or_name"):
+ init_kwargs["auth_model"] = policy.auth_model_or_name
+ if hasattr(policy, "owner_field_name"):
+ init_kwargs["owner_field_name"] = policy.owner_field_name
+ try:
+ policy = policy.class(self.model, init_kwargs)
+ except TypeError:
+ policy = None
+
+ if not policy:
+ return queryset
+
+ allowed_queryset = policy.instances_user_has_permission_for(
 self.request.user, self.permission_required
 )
+ return queryset.filter(pkin=allowed_queryset.values("pk"))
 
 def get_form_class(self):
 return get_document_form(self.model)
